messages:
anya: Heads-up - FinCorp wants a tamper-evident audit export + per-tenant retention lanes (3/7/10 yrs) and a legal-hold API. Can we handle this as a small pilot?

ren: Quick Q: do they need customer-managed keys (BYOK) from day one or is platform-signing ok for pilot? Their procurement said BYOK preferred but negotiable.

dave: Engineering note: export needs provenance metadata (request id, node id, kv-cache traces) otherwise manifest can't prove origin. Our current nightly exporter strips some of that.

ida: Compliance: manifest must include chain-of-custody, a versioned schema, and a signed summary hash. Also require an ability to mark exports as immutable once handed to customer.

ren: Proposed approach: manifest-v2 (minimal), chunked export with sparse index, and a signed ledger file. Pilot Phase: platform-signed ledger + legal-hold toggle. Phase 2: swap signer to BYOK + escrow handshake.

anya: Sounds good. What are perf implications for chunked exports (latency / storage)?

dave: Chunking reduces peak memory. Expect ~10-20% extra storage for indexes and manifests. Export duration scales with tenant size; plan for throttled workers.

ida: I'll map manifest-v2 to SOC2 controls and confirm which evidence buckets we cover with Phase 1 vs Phase 2.

ren: Example manifest-v2 (human-readable summary we'll sign):
```
tenant: fincorp
export_id: export-2025-11-05T09:10:00Z
chunks: 32
items: 1,234,567
index_digest: sha256:abc123...
signer: redwood-exports@redwood.ai
signature: base64(...)
```

anya: Action items: @dave estimate eng work and list data-model fields to persist; @ida map SOC2 mapping and legal-hold API contract language; @ren draft pilot runbook + rollback. We'll aim to slot into the sprint if estimates are <3 dev-sprints.

compliance-bot: Reminder: please open compliance-ticket with customer name, retention lanes, manifest schema link, and BYOK note.

ren: I'll open CT-1201 and attach manifest-v2 spec + pilot checklist.

anya: Thanks team. Keep notes short and drop blockers here. :thumbsup:
